method: read-only live inspection of the w541 rig over SSH: sysfs topology walk, timed disable-register sweep, journalctl (kernel + service), manual adb server restart test, lsusb -v control-transfer probe, slot arithmetic

root_cause.title: xHCI device-slot exhaustion on Intel 8-Series controller (32 slots)
evidence: kernel: 'usb 1-2.2: Not enough host controller resources for new device state' + 'can't set config #1, error -12', retrying every ~67s for hours
exactly 32 devices on buses 1+3 at audit time (21 + 11)
each A16 = 5 cascaded Realtek 4-port chips, each enumerating on USB2 AND as USB3 companion: 20 hub slots for two A16s
stuck watches answer lsusb -v control transfers (live) but have no interface directories (unconfigured)

findings.title: UI power dots read a cold cache no one fills since 5082d12 removed empty-port polling; registers meanwhile match mo's LED counts
'disable reads hang seconds / renegotiate the hub' does not reproduce: 40 registers in 0.8s total (3-90ms each) on a quiet bus; prior hangs were contention with the F1 retry storm and uhubctl scans

sweep re-implemented poweroff with a 3-36s adb-drop wait before the VBUS cut (port.poweroff documents cut-immediately) and stamps safe_off on adb-drop, which also fires on reboot -> false 'shelved', fleet drained
reconnect/onboard latencies are wait-loop artefacts: 15s poll granularity (adb_wait_seconds) and >=90s blind waits on an adb server that can never list a slot-starved watch
adb-wedge self-heal keys on adb interface descriptors, which slot-starved watches lack -> blind to the active failure; server restart correctly changes nothing (tested)
the 8th-watch 'brownout' is slot exhaustion at the USB layer; hubs are self-powered (bmAttributes=e0, kernel power budget not involved); electrical residue is mo's domain
shelved-port disable registers agree with dark LEDs: yesterday's VBUS cuts did cut; the shelve failure was watches rebooting before the cut (F4), not the cut
stuck inventory: KW88 (1-2.2), narwhal (1-1.3.4.3), sawfish (1-1.3.3.3) slot-starved live; ZenWatch GCNZ (1-1.4.2) starved in 0afe mode; two ZenWatches configured in 0afe but invisible to fastboot

disproven: stale-corpse-node theory for the current stuck watches (they answer control transfers)
A16 cannot switch VBUS on direct-host wiring (registers track LEDs)
electrical brownout as the primary 8th-watch mechanism (F7)
adb server wedge as the current reconnect blocker (F6)
bus-powered hub kernel power-budget refusal (bmAttributes=e0 self-powered)

fix_directions.A: free controller slots: unbind idle SS companion trees (+10), and/or move A16 uplinks to USB2-only host ports, and/or route hub ports to EHCI via XUSB2PR (removes ceiling entirely); operational shelving discipline + gauge as interim
fix_directions.B: single serialized background register sweep (~1s/40 ports) feeding power_cache; UI dot = register; xHCI slot gauge with warning in header
fix_directions.C: udev netlink event-driven discovery replacing 15s/90s polling; 'enumerated but unconfigured' becomes a detected, surfaced state
fix_directions.D: one poweroff implementation (port.poweroff path): synchronous delivery then immediate VBUS cut; uptime-based verification; per-watch halt behaviour recorded in registry
fix_directions.E: self-heal splits into: interfaces-present-but-server-blind -> restart server; enumerated-without-interfaces -> report slot exhaustion

open_questions_for_mo: target concurrency: N-live-rest-shelved, or all 32 sockets enumerated at once? (decides A1/A2 vs A3)
go-ahead for the reversible unbind falsification test on 3-2, then a one-port VBUS/LED check with the SS side unbound
are A16 #2's physical per-port buttons all ON? (audit assumed so)
re-evaluate the measured voltage droop knowing config-refusals were concurrent
